nodes.title: Keep one progress number in a signal
nodes.why: The percentage label, the fill width, aria-valuenow and the color class all read this value, so one update from a button moves every binding together.
nodes.alternative: Store the width string and the color class in their own fields and set them next to the number in inc() and dec().
nodes.tradeoff: Deriving everything from one number rules out a label and bar that disagree; the cost is calling progress() in each binding instead of reading a plain field.

nodes.title: Derive the color class from the value
nodes.why: barClass turns the number into bar red, bar orange or bar green in one place, the template binds it with [class], and the string is recalculated only when progress changes.
nodes.alternative: Write the three conditions inline with [ngClass] in the template, or return the class from a getter that runs on every check.
nodes.tradeoff: One computed keeps the template to a single binding and caches the result; inline conditions show the thresholds in the markup but repeat them anywhere else the color is needed.

nodes.title: Test the thresholds from low to high
nodes.why: The red check above returns first, so this line only sees values of 34 and up; <= 66 makes 66 orange and 67 green, as the hint under the bar states.
nodes.alternative: Test each band with both bounds, such as value >= 34 && value <= 66, so the checks can run in any order.
nodes.tradeoff: Ordered early returns are shorter, but reordering them changes the result; two-sided ranges survive reordering at the cost of repeating every bound.

nodes.title: Cap the increase at 100 inside the update
nodes.why: update reads the current value and Math.min caps the result, so pressing +10% at 100 stores 100 again instead of 110 and the label never reads 110%.
nodes.alternative: Disable the +10% button at 100 and skip the clamp in inc().
nodes.tradeoff: The clamp keeps the stored value valid for any caller; disabling the button as well would show that the limit is reached, which this solution leaves out.

nodes.title: Clamp the stored value at zero
nodes.why: Math.max holds the value at 0, so -10% at 0 changes nothing, and the label, the width and aria-valuenow never show a negative number.
nodes.alternative: Let the number go below zero and clamp only the width binding in the template.
nodes.tradeoff: Clamping the stored number keeps every reader honest; clamping only the display would draw an empty bar while the label and aria-valuenow show -10.
